symptoms.question: Is the fuel level often very low or close to empty when you experience problems? (yes/no)
Does the car accelerate more slowly than usual, even with more throttle? (yes/no)
Does the engine hesitate or stumble when accelerating or climbing hills? (yes/no)
Do you feel the engine misfire or jerk during acceleration? (yes/no)
Do you see dark or black smoke from the exhaust when accelerating? (yes/no)
Has fuel consumption increased noticeably without a change in driving style? (yes/no)
Is the engine harder to start when it is hot than when it is cold? (yes/no)
Has the fuel filter not been replaced for a long time (or you do not know when)? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Low fuel level with hesitation under load can indicate fuel starvation, especially in corners or on hills.
rules.advice: Avoid running the tank very low and refuel. If the problem remains, have the fuel pick-up and pump checked.

rules.diagnosis: Hesitation and poor acceleration with an old fuel filter suggest restricted fuel flow.
rules.advice: Replacing the fuel filter is a relatively simple maintenance step that may restore performance.

rules.diagnosis: Black exhaust smoke and high fuel consumption indicate a rich fuel mixture.
rules.advice: Have the engine management system checked for sensor faults or leaking injectors to avoid damage to the catalytic converter.

rules.diagnosis: Difficult hot starts with normal fuel level can be caused by fuel vapour or weak fuel pressure.
rules.advice: Mention the hot-start behaviour to a mechanic; checking fuel pressure and injector leakage may be necessary.

rules.diagnosis: Misfire during acceleration with a check engine light suggests injector or mixture problems on one or more cylinders.
rules.advice: Avoid heavy acceleration and have the fault codes read to identify which cylinder is affected.
